notes: Functionally correct, with thorough end-to-end and single-object-root tests, but the squashfs New/NewObject fallback logic and the zip Open special case for offsets past the end are convoluted.
Production code is identical to the reference, plus a zip unit test, a mksquashfs end-to-end test, a hostile-archive escape test and docs.

Essentially matches the reference in zip and squashfs with clean range/seek handling and good unit tests, though it has no hostile-archive test and silently treats a symlink as a regular file when StatT is missing.
Ignores the ctx config in zip, and the squashfs symlink objects neither report the target length nor read back the target; no tests.

The zip side reads Links from context.Background(), so --links set in a context is ignored; squashfs depends on a probably-missing Readlink interface and its link Open ignores range options; no tests.

Squashfs depends on an unsupported Readlink interface, skipped symlinks are counted in the 'escape the archive' message, and members under any symlink are dropped even without --links; Size re-reads the member on every call and no tests were added.

Over-engineered SafeLinkTarget filtering goes against the spec: it drops absolute and '..' targets and hides regular .rclonelink members whose content is not a 'safe' target, adding much unrequested complexity.

Works and handles name collisions with strong tests including the hostile copy, but a squashfs symlink with an empty target makes the whole List fail, and the zip root is matched before the suffix is added.

Clean, correct implementation with the suffix added before root filtering and good unit and hostile-copy tests; it logs once per skipped link and does not exclude directory entries from the symlink check.

Correct for both backends and also adds regular-file-wins collision handling, a bounded eager target read and a shared open helper; it logs once per symlink rather than a summary, and a zip root naming a symlink is matched before the suffix is added.
